prompt.context: Your client is a record producer looking to bring a new music act to the United States. While traveling through Scandinavia he came across a Swedish Death Metal band he thinks would be a perfect fit for his label. There are currently no Swedish Death Metal bands on US labels and all of their music must be imported from Europe.
prompt.question: Advise the client whether this is a good idea and give him some launch process suggestions.

clarifying_info.q: What is the difference between an import versus a domestic release?
clarifying_info.a: Imports eat into the margin of the album for the record company and there is no way to price higher.
Yes, this metric includes digital sales.

clarifying_info.q: Is there data on the size of the Swedish Death Metal market specifically?
clarifying_info.a: There are no reliable metrics in the US as this is a relatively new market. The larger Death Metal market will serve as a proxy.

framework: 1. How to introduce the SDM band to the US market: (a) Album sales, (b) Touring as opening or headlining act, (c) Late night television appearances, (d) Music blogs
2. Market size: (a) Total albums sold in US, (b) Size of Death Metal market, (c) Share of the market the SDM band can capture
3. Customer: (a) Are Death Metal fans willing to make the transition to Swedish Death Metal?
4. Financials: (a) Will the record label be able to charge standard pricing for a new album?
5. Risks: (a) Band breaks up, (b) Drugs/alcohol abuse

questions.prompt: Last year 150 million albums were sold in the United States. 13% of them were Death Metal. How many Death Metal albums were sold?
questions.guidance: Straightforward percentage calculation. Candidates may round 19.5m to 20m.

math.setup: Total US album sales × Death Metal share
math.answer: 19.5 million Death Metal albums sold (can round to 20 million)

questions.prompt: The Death Metal market is segmented into three groups: hardcore, average, and casual fans. They comprise 20%, 30%, and 50% of the population, respectively. Each group buys 4, 2, and 1.2 albums per person per year. Solve for the size of each group and the number of albums purchased by each group.
questions.guidance: Candidates often confuse the size of the population with the 20 million albums sold. If the candidate multiplies 20m by 20%/30%/50% directly, guide them toward solving for the population first using a single variable.

math.setup: Let x = total Death Metal fan population. Weighted average albums per person = 4(0.20) + 2(0.30) + 1.2(0.50). Set total albums = x × weighted average = 20m.
math.answer: 10 million total fans; 2m hardcore (8m albums), 3m average (6m albums), 5m casual (6m albums)

questions.prompt: We would like to know the breakeven volume of albums for three marketing programs. Each album is priced at $12. The three marketing options are: Internet — $300k; Internet & Radio — $1m; Internet, Radio & TV — $2m. What is the breakeven volume for each option?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask about variable and fixed costs before calculating. Variable costs: CD Manufacturing $2/CD, CD Distribution $3/CD, Royalties $3/CD. No other fixed costs. Calculate contribution margin first, then breakeven for each plan.

math.setup: Contribution Margin = Price − Variable Costs. Breakeven = Fixed Cost (marketing spend) ÷ Contribution Margin.
math.answer: 75k units (Internet), 250k units (Internet & Radio), 500k units (Internet, Radio & TV)

questions.prompt: Which marketing option would you choose?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask whether the marketing plans target specific fan segments. Each plan maps to one segment: Hardcore = Internet, Average = Radio, Casual = TV. Candidate should relate breakeven volumes to the 10m potential customers. Internet plan requires ~3.75% market share of hardcore segment (2m fans); Internet & Radio requires ~2.5% of hardcore+average (5m fans); Internet, Radio & TV requires 5% of all 10m fans. Since SDM is entirely new to the US and capturing significant share in a new sub-genre is very unlikely, the Internet-only plan targeting hardcore fans is the most realistic. Candidate is not expected to calculate market share percentages but earns credit for doing so.

math.setup: Market share required = Breakeven units ÷ Relevant fan population
math.answer: Internet-only plan; targeting hardcore fans is most achievable for a new sub-genre

brainstorming.prompt: How should the client introduce the SDM band to the US market?

categories.name: Digital / Online
ideas: Internet-only marketing campaign targeting hardcore Death Metal fans
Social media presence and streaming platforms

categories.name: Live Performance
ideas: Touring as opening act for an established Death Metal band
Headlining small-venue tour to build grassroots following

categories.name: Label Strategy
ideas: Pilot launch with a single before signing a longer-term contract
Partner with established label for distribution to reduce import margin drag

recommendation: The client should bring the SDM act to the US using the Internet-only marketing plan targeting hardcore Death Metal fans.

This is the first Swedish Death Metal act to be based in the US; Death Metal is a niche market and attracting hardcore fans is the best path towards gaining market share and expanding into other fan groups.
risks: Band could be a complete flop, break up, or face issues such as drug or alcohol addiction.
Musical taste is very subjective; US fans may not transition from Death Metal to Swedish Death Metal.
Capturing significant market share in a sub-genre entirely new to the US is uncertain.
next_steps: Explore a pilot launch with singles before signing a longer-term contract.
Explore other revenue-generating opportunities such as touring as an opener for an established act.
Consider late night television appearances to build awareness beyond the hardcore segment.
